source.text: הִנֵּ֨ה עַל־הֶהָרִ֜ים רַגְלֵ֤י מְבַשֵּׂר֙ מַשְׁמִ֣יעַ שָׁל֔וֹם חָגִּ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה חַגַּ֖יִךְ שַׁלְּמִ֣י נְדָרָ֑יִךְ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוֹסִ֥יף ע֛וֹד לַֽעֲבָר־בָּ֥ךְ בְּלִיַּ֖עַל כֻּלֹּ֥ה נִכְרָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, on the mountains [the] feet of [one who] brings good news, [who] announces peace! Celebrate, Judah, your festivals; fulfill your vows; for not again will pass through you [the] worthless [one]; all of him is cut off.

en.L: Look, on the mountains [are the] feet of [the] bearer of good news, announcing peace! \q Celebrate your festivals, Judah; fulfill your vows; \q for the worthless one will never again pass through you; he is completely cut off.
en.B: Look! On the mountains, the feet of one who brings good news! He calls out peace. \q Celebrate your festivals, Judah, and fulfill your vows, \q for the worthless one will never again march through you; he is cut off completely.
en.R: Look! A messenger with good news is coming over the mountains. He announces peace. \q People of Judah, celebrate your festivals, and keep the promises you made to God. \q The wicked enemy will never again march through your land. He has been completely destroyed.

vi.L: Kìa, trên các núi, chân của người đem tin lành, người công bố bình an! \q Hỡi Giu-đa, hãy cử hành các kỳ lễ của ngươi; hãy làm trọn các lời khấn hứa của ngươi; \q vì kẻ vô dụng kia sẽ không bao giờ đi qua ngươi nữa; nó đã bị diệt trừ hoàn toàn.
vi.B: Kìa! Trên các núi, bước chân của người đem tin lành! Người loan báo bình an. \q Hỡi Giu-đa, hãy cử hành các kỳ lễ và làm trọn lời khấn hứa, \q vì kẻ gian ác kia sẽ không bao giờ kéo quân qua ngươi nữa; nó đã bị diệt trừ hoàn toàn.
vi.R: Hãy xem! Một người đưa tin vui đang vượt qua các núi mà đến. Người loan báo bình an. \q Hỡi dân Giu-đa, hãy cử hành các kỳ lễ, và giữ những lời hứa các ngươi đã khấn với Đức Chúa Trời. \q Kẻ thù gian ác sẽ không bao giờ kéo quân qua xứ các ngươi nữa. Nó đã bị tiêu diệt hoàn toàn.

decisions.choice: This verse is 2:1 in the Hebrew text, 1:15 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins chapter 2 with the messenger of good news. Many Bibles end chapter 1 with this verse, numbering it 1:15, so their 2:1-13 is 2:2-14 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Nahum is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: the feet of one who brings good news, announcing peace: the words of Isaiah 52:7
decisions.reason: Isaiah 52:7 says: "How lovely on the mountains are the feet of the one who brings good news, announcing peace", and goes on to the news that Zion's God reigns. Nahum uses the same words, beginning with "Look". News came by runners, and the watchers saw the messenger crossing the hills (2 Samuel 18:24-27). Here the news is that Nineveh has fallen and Judah is free. Paul quotes Isaiah's form of the line of those who preach the gospel (Romans 10:15).

decisions.choice: celebrate your festivals, fulfill your vows: worship that the danger had prevented
decisions.reason: Judah's feasts at the temple (Deuteronomy 16:16) can be kept again in peace. A vow was a promise made to God in time of trouble, to be paid with an offering once he had answered (Psalm 66:13-14; Jonah 2:10). Judah is told to pay what it promised, because the answer has come.

decisions.choice: the worthless one: the Assyrian
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in 1:11 of the one who plotted evil against the LORD. Here it stands for the Assyrian invader, who will "never again pass through" Judah, that is, invade it (compare Isaiah 52:1, "never again will the uncircumcised enter you").

decisions.choice: the Isaiah 52:7 wording at each level, with "Look" for Isaiah's "How lovely"
decisions.reason: The shared words are worded as in Isaiah 52:7 at each level: "[the] feet of [the] bearer of good news, announcing peace" (Literal), "the feet of one who brings good news! He calls out peace" (Balanced) and "A messenger with good news is coming over the mountains. He announces peace" (Readable). Nahum's "Look" stands where Isaiah has "How lovely", and Nahum does not go on to Isaiah's further lines.

decisions.choice: keep the promises you made to God; The wicked enemy
decisions.reason: Readable explains "vows" (m3) and says "the wicked enemy" for "the worthless one" (m4).

decisions.choice: the published Isaiah 52:7 at each level ("chân của người đem tin lành, người công bố bình an" L; "bước chân của người đem tin lành! Người loan báo bình an" B; "Một người đưa tin vui đang vượt qua các núi mà đến" R), with "Kìa" for Isaiah's "How lovely"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision names Isaiah 52:7 and the terms note asks that Nahum 2:1 reuse it. "Người đem tin lành" is lowercase, the bearer of news, not "Tin Lành" the gospel. Judah is "ngươi" here, as one person addressed.

decisions.choice: "kẻ vô dụng" (L); "kẻ gian ác" (B); "kẻ thù gian ác" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: the Assyrian; the Hebrew word ("belial") is a quality, not a name, so Vietnamese does not transliterate it.

source.text: עָלָ֥ה מֵפִ֛יץ עַל־פָּנַ֖יִךְ נָצ֣וֹר מְצֻרָ֑ה צַפֵּה־דֶ֨רֶךְ֙ חַזֵּ֣ק מָתְנַ֔יִם אַמֵּ֥ץ כֹּ֖חַ מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Has come up [one who] scatters against your face. Guard [the] rampart! Watch [the] road! Strengthen [the] loins! Make strength firm exceedingly!

en.L: One who scatters has come up against you; guard the rampart! \q Watch the road; brace [your] loins; \q make [your] strength very firm!
en.B: One who scatters is coming up against you. Guard the ramparts! \q Watch the road! Brace yourself! \q Gather all your strength!
en.R: Nineveh, an enemy is coming to scatter your people. Guard your walls! \q Watch the roads! Get ready to fight! \q Use all the strength you have!

vi.L: Kẻ phân tán đã đi lên nghịch cùng ngươi; hãy canh giữ thành lũy! \q Hãy canh chừng đường lối; hãy thắt chặt lưng [ngươi]; \q hãy làm cho sức [ngươi] thật vững mạnh!
vi.B: Kẻ đánh tan đang tiến lên đánh ngươi. Hãy canh giữ thành lũy! \q Hãy canh chừng đường sá! Hãy nai nịt sẵn sàng! \q Hãy dồn hết sức lực!
vi.R: Hỡi Ni-ni-ve, kẻ thù đang đến để làm dân ngươi tan tác. Hãy canh giữ tường thành! \q Hãy canh chừng các con đường! Hãy sẵn sàng chiến đấu! \q Hãy dùng hết sức lực ngươi có!

decisions.choice: This verse is 2:2 in the Hebrew text, 2:1 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: Because the Hebrew text begins chapter 2 one verse earlier (see the note at 2:1), Hebrew 2:2-14 is 2:1-13 in many Bibles. Open Word Bible follows the Hebrew numbering.

decisions.choice: against you: Nineveh, told to prepare for the siege
decisions.reason: "You" is feminine singular, the city of Nineveh (verse 9). The commands are a call to arms, but they are ironic: however well she guards her walls, she will fall. Verses 2-14 describe the attack on the city as if the prophet were watching it.

decisions.choice: one who scatters: the attacker who will drive the people of Nineveh apart
decisions.reason: The word means "one who scatters" (compare 3:18, "your people are scattered on the mountains"). With a slight change of vowels it could be "a war club" or "hammer", the word used in Jeremiah 51:20. The attackers were the Babylonians and the Medes (see the note at 1:1).

decisions.choice: Brace yourself (B); Get ready to fight (R); Gather all your strength (B)
decisions.reason: "Strengthen the loins" means to get ready for hard effort, as one tied up long clothes before action (1 Kings 18:46). Balanced and Readable give the sense. Readable names Nineveh as the one addressed (m2).

decisions.choice: Nineveh is addressed as "ngươi" and spoken of as "nó"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: Nineveh, told to prepare for the siege; the terms note gives a foreign city "ngươi" in address and "nó" in the third person, though the Hebrew pictures her as a woman (2:8).

source.text: כִּ֣י שָׁ֤ב יְהוָה֙ אֶת־גְּא֣וֹן יַעֲקֹ֔ב כִּגְא֖וֹן יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י בְקָקוּם֙ בֹּֽקְקִ֔ים וּזְמֹרֵיהֶ֖ם שִׁחֵֽתוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For Yahweh is restoring the majesty of Jacob like [the] majesty of Israel, for plunderers have plundered them, and their branches they have destroyed.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is restoring the majesty of Jacob \q like the majesty of Israel, \q for plunderers have plundered them \q and ruined their branches.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is restoring the glory of Jacob, \q like the glory of Israel, \q though plunderers have stripped them bare \q and ruined their vines.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is going to bring back the glory of Jacob's people, \q the glory of Israel, \q even though enemies have robbed them \q and stripped them like a vine.

vi.L: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang khôi phục sự uy nghi của Gia-cốp \q như sự uy nghi của Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q vì những kẻ cướp phá đã cướp phá họ \q và làm hư hại các nhánh nho của họ.
vi.B: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang khôi phục vinh quang của Gia-cốp, \q như vinh quang của Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q dù quân cướp phá đã vơ vét sạch họ \q và tàn phá các cây nho của họ.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đem vinh quang trở lại cho dân Gia-cốp, \q là vinh quang của Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q dù quân thù đã cướp bóc họ \q và lột trụi họ như lột cây nho.

decisions.choice: a word of hope for God's people in the middle of the battle
decisions.reason: The verse breaks into the description of the attack on Nineveh to give the reason for it: the LORD is restoring his people. The first word (*ki*) may be "for" or "surely"; the second *ki* may be "for" or "though": Israel will be restored though, or because, it has been plundered.

decisions.choice: the majesty of Jacob like the majesty of Israel
decisions.reason: The word usually means pride or majesty; here it is the good pride of a people who belong to God (Psalm 47:5). "Jacob" and "Israel" may be two names for the one people, or "Jacob" may be Judah and "Israel" the northern kingdom that Assyria destroyed, so that both are restored together.

decisions.choice: plunderers ... their branches: Israel as a vine stripped bare
decisions.reason: Israel is often pictured as a vine that God planted (Psalm 80:9-17; Isaiah 5:1-7). Enemies have broken down its branches and stripped it. The plunderers are the Assyrians, who are about to be plundered in their turn (verse 10).

decisions.choice: glory (B, R); vines (B); stripped them like a vine (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "glory" for the word that can also mean "pride" (m2), to keep its good sense. Readable makes the vine a comparison (m3).

source.text: מָגֵ֨ן גִּבֹּרֵ֜יהוּ מְאָדָּ֗ם אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֨יִל֙ מְתֻלָּעִ֔ים בְּאֵשׁ־פְּלָד֥וֹת הָרֶ֖כֶב בְּי֣וֹם הֲכִינ֑וֹ וְהַבְּרֹשִׁ֖ים הָרְעָֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: The shield of his mighty men [is] made red; men of valor [are] clothed in scarlet; with fire of steel [are] the chariots on [the] day of his preparing, and the cypresses are made to quiver.

en.L: The shields of his warriors [are] reddened; the men of valor [are] in scarlet; \q the chariots [flash] with the fire of steel on the day of his preparing, \q and the cypress [spears] are brandished.
en.B: The shields of his warriors are red; his soldiers are dressed in scarlet. \q The chariots flash like fire with steel on the day he musters them, \q and the spears of cypress wood are brandished.
en.R: The enemy soldiers carry red shields and wear scarlet uniforms. \q Their chariots flash like fire as they line up for battle. \q Their spears are raised and ready.

vi.L: Khiên của các dũng sĩ nó [nhuộm] đỏ; các chiến binh [mặc] áo đỏ thắm; \q các xe chiến mã [lóe sáng] như lửa thép trong ngày nó dàn trận, \q và các [ngọn giáo bằng gỗ] bách vung lên.
vi.B: Khiên của các dũng sĩ nó đỏ rực; quân lính nó mặc áo đỏ thắm. \q Các xe chiến mã lóe thép sáng như lửa trong ngày nó dàn quân, \q và những ngọn giáo bằng gỗ bách vung lên.
vi.R: Quân thù cầm khiên đỏ và mặc quân phục đỏ thắm. \q Xe chiến mã của chúng lóe sáng như lửa khi dàn trận. \q Giáo của chúng giương lên sẵn sàng.

decisions.choice: red shields and scarlet clothes: the attacking army
decisions.reason: "His" is the attacker, the "one who scatters" of verse 2. The red may be paint or leather on the shields, or the color of blood. Ezekiel 23:14 speaks of the Babylonians pictured in red. The scarlet uniforms make the army stand out in its splendor.

decisions.choice: the fire of steel: the gleaming metal of the chariots
alternatives: the chariots are like flaming torches
decisions.reason: The word translated "steel" is used only here, and its meaning is uncertain. It may be the metal fittings of the chariots flashing in the sun, or, by a change of letters, "torches". Either way the chariots shine like fire.

decisions.choice: the cypress [spears] are brandished
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the cypresses are made to quiver", probably spears with shafts of cypress wood, shaken as the army gets ready. The Greek translation reads "the horsemen", which differs from the Hebrew by one letter, and pictures the horses prancing. The translation follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: on the day he musters them (B); as they line up for battle (R); spears of cypress wood (B)
decisions.reason: "The day of his preparing" is the day the commander gets his army ready for battle; Balanced says "musters them", Readable "line up for battle". Literal brackets "spears", which the Hebrew implies (m3).

source.text: בַּֽחוּצוֹת֙ יִתְהוֹלְל֣וּ הָרֶ֔כֶב יִֽשְׁתַּקְשְׁק֖וּן בָּרְחֹב֑וֹת מַרְאֵיהֶן֙ כַּלַּפִּידִ֔ם כַּבְּרָקִ֖ים יְרוֹצֵֽצוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: In the streets drive madly the chariots; they rush back and forth in the squares; their appearance [is] like torches; like lightning they run about.

en.L: In the streets the chariots drive madly; \q they rush back and forth in the squares; \q their appearance [is] like torches; \q like lightning they dart about.
en.B: The chariots race madly through the streets \q and rush back and forth in the squares. \q They look like flaming torches; \q they dart about like lightning.
en.R: The chariots race wildly through the streets. \q They rush back and forth through the open places. \q They flash like torches. \q They dart about like lightning.

vi.L: Trên các đường phố, xe chiến mã phóng điên cuồng; \q chúng lao tới lui trong các quảng trường; \q hình dạng chúng [như] những ngọn đuốc; \q chúng chạy như chớp nhoáng.
vi.B: Xe chiến mã phóng điên cuồng qua các đường phố \q và lao tới lui trong các quảng trường. \q Trông chúng như những ngọn đuốc rực lửa; \q chúng lao đi như tia chớp.
vi.R: Xe chiến mã phóng điên cuồng qua các đường phố. \q Chúng lao tới lao lui qua những nơi trống trải. \q Chúng lóe sáng như những ngọn đuốc. \q Chúng lao đi như tia chớp.

decisions.choice: the chariots in the streets: the attackers' chariots
alternatives: Nineveh's chariots rushing about in panic
decisions.reason: The chariots are most likely those of the attackers of verse 4, racing through the streets and open spaces outside the walls or bursting into the city. Some read them as Nineveh's own chariots rushing about in panic. The poem gives quick pictures without saying whose they are.

decisions.choice: the open places
decisions.reason: The word for "squares" means broad places, the open spaces of a city where people gathered; Readable says "open places".

source.text: יִזְכֹּר֙ אַדִּירָ֔יו יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ בַּהֲלִֽיכָתָ֑ם יְמַֽהֲרוּ֙ חֽוֹמָתָ֔הּ וְהֻכַ֖ן הַסֹּכֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: He remembers his nobles; they stumble in their going; they hurry [to] her wall, and the covering is set up.

en.L: He remembers his nobles; \q they stumble in their marching; \q they hurry to her wall, \q and the protective shield is set up.
en.B: He calls up his officers; \q they stumble as they advance. \q They rush to the city wall, \q and the siege shelter is set in place.
en.R: The enemy commander calls for his officers. \q They stumble as they hurry forward. \q They rush to the city wall \q and set up a shelter to protect the attackers.

vi.L: Nó nhớ đến các tướng lĩnh của nó; \q họ vấp ngã trong lúc tiến quân; \q họ vội vã đến tường thành, \q và tấm khiên che đã được dựng lên.
vi.B: Nó gọi các tướng lĩnh của mình đến; \q họ vấp ngã trong khi tiến lên. \q Họ lao đến tường thành, \q và mái che công thành được dựng lên.
vi.R: Tướng chỉ huy quân thù gọi các sĩ quan của mình. \q Họ vấp ngã khi vội vàng tiến lên. \q Họ lao đến tường thành \q và dựng một mái che để bảo vệ những người tấn công.

decisions.choice: he remembers his nobles: the commander of the attack calls up his officers
alternatives: the king of Nineveh calling up his nobles to defend the wall
decisions.reason: The verse does not say who "he" is. Because the "covering" at the end is a device used by attackers, he is most likely the commander of verse 4, calling up his best troops for the assault on the wall. Some take him as the king of Nineveh calling his nobles to defend the city, who stumble in their panic.

decisions.choice: the covering: a shelter protecting those who attack the wall
decisions.reason: The word means something that covers or screens. Assyrian art shows wheeled shelters covered with hides or wicker, which protected soldiers working a battering ram or digging at the foot of a wall. It is the attackers' equipment, now used against the Assyrians themselves.

decisions.choice: He calls up (B); The enemy commander (R); the siege shelter (B); a shelter to protect the attackers (R)
decisions.reason: "Remembers" here means calls to mind and so calls up; Balanced and Readable say so. Readable names the commander and the purpose of the shelter, following the reading in m1.

records.literal_gloss: The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace melts.

en.L: The gates of the rivers are opened, \q and the palace melts away.
en.B: The river gates are thrown open, \q and the palace gives way.
en.R: The gates by the rivers are opened, \q and the palace falls apart.

vi.L: Các cửa sông được mở ra, \q và cung điện tan chảy.
vi.B: Các cửa sông bị mở toang, \q và cung điện sụp đổ.
vi.R: Các cửa bên sông được mở ra, \q và cung điện đổ sập.

decisions.choice: the gates of the rivers: the gates or sluices where the city's waters ran
decisions.reason: Nineveh lay on the Tigris, and the Khosr river ran through the city; canals and dams brought water to it. "The gates of the rivers" may be city gates beside the waterways or sluice gates that controlled them. A later Greek historian tells that a flood broke down part of Nineveh's wall during the siege; Nahum's words may refer to waters let loose against the city, or to gates opened to the attackers.

decisions.choice: the palace melts away: it collapses, or its people lose heart
alternatives: the people of the palace melt with fear
decisions.reason: The verb means to melt or dissolve. It may describe the palace collapsing as water undermines its mud-brick walls, or, as often with this verb, the terror of those inside (Joshua 2:9, 24).

decisions.choice: gives way (B); falls apart (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the palace "melts": it gives way and falls apart, which keeps both senses in m2 open.

source.text: וְהֻצַּ֖ב גֻּלְּתָ֣ה הֹֽעֲלָ֑תָה וְאַמְהֹתֶ֗יהָ מְנַֽהֲגוֹת֙ כְּק֣וֹל יוֹנִ֔ים מְתֹפְפֹ֖ת עַל־לִבְבֵהֶֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And it is fixed: she is uncovered, she is carried away; and her slave women [are] moaning like [the] sound of doves, beating on their hearts.

en.L: And it is decided: she is stripped, she is carried away, \q and her slave women moan like the sound of doves, \q beating on their hearts.
en.B: It is decreed: she is stripped and carried away, \q and her servant women moan like doves \q and beat their breasts.
en.R: It has been decided: Nineveh will be stripped and carried away. \q Her servant women moan like doves \q and beat their breasts in grief.

vi.L: Điều ấy đã được định: nó bị lột trần, nó bị bắt đi, \q và các nữ tì của nó rên rỉ như tiếng chim bồ câu, \q đấm vào lòng mình.
vi.B: Điều ấy đã được định: nó bị lột trần và bị bắt đi, \q các tớ gái của nó rên rỉ như chim bồ câu \q và đấm ngực.
vi.R: Việc đã được định rồi: Ni-ni-ve sẽ bị lột trần và bị bắt đi. \q Các tớ gái của nó rên rỉ như chim bồ câu \q và đấm ngực than khóc.

decisions.choice: it is decided: a word whose meaning is uncertain
alternatives: the name or title of Nineveh's queen
decisions.reason: The first word is unclear. It may be a verb, "it is fixed" or "it is decreed", as taken here. Others have read it as the name or title of a queen of Nineveh, or have changed its letters to read "the beauty" or "the lady".

decisions.choice: she is stripped, she is carried away: the city, or its queen or goddess
decisions.reason: "She" may be Nineveh, pictured as a woman, the city's queen, or the statue of its goddess, which conquerors carried off as plunder (Isaiah 46:1-2; Jeremiah 48:7). Stripping pictures shame and captivity (3:5).

decisions.choice: moaning like doves, beating their breasts: mourning
decisions.reason: The low, sad cry of the dove was a picture of grief (Isaiah 38:14; 59:11). Beating the breast was a sign of sorrow (Isaiah 32:12; Luke 23:48).

decisions.choice: slave women (L); servant women (B, R); hearts (L); breasts (B, R)
decisions.reason: As with the word for a male servant, Literal says "slave" and Balanced and Readable "servant". The Hebrew says "hearts"; English says "beat their breasts". Readable names Nineveh as "she", the most likely reading of m2.

decisions.choice: "nữ tì" (L); "tớ gái" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The English moves from "slave women" (L) to "servant women" (B, R); Vietnamese "nữ tì" keeps the bound status at Literal without the harsher "nô lệ", which the terms note keeps for slavery itself.

source.text: וְנִינְוֵ֥ה כִבְרֵֽכַת־מַ֖יִם מִ֣ימֵי הִ֑יא וְהֵ֣מָּה נָסִ֔ים עִמְד֥וּ עֲמֹ֖דוּ וְאֵ֥ין מַפְנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Nineveh [was] like a pool of water from [the] days of her, and they [are] fleeing. Stop! Stop! But there is not [one who] turns back.

en.L: And Nineveh [is] like a pool of water from her days, \q and they flee. \q "Stop! Stop!" But no one turns back.
en.B: Nineveh has been like a pool of water since ancient days, \q and now its people flee. \q "Halt! Halt!" But no one turns back.
en.R: Since long ago Nineveh has been like a pool full of water. \q Now its people are running away like water draining out. \q Someone shouts, "Stop! Stop!" But no one turns back.

vi.L: Ni-ni-ve [như] một hồ nước từ những ngày của nó, \q và chúng bỏ chạy. \q "Dừng lại! Dừng lại!" Nhưng chẳng ai quay lại.
vi.B: Từ xưa Ni-ni-ve vẫn như một hồ nước, \q mà nay dân nó bỏ chạy. \q "Đứng lại! Đứng lại!" Nhưng chẳng ai quay lại.
vi.R: Từ lâu Ni-ni-ve như một hồ đầy nước. \q Nay dân nó chạy trốn như nước chảy tràn ra ngoài. \q Có người kêu lên: "Dừng lại! Dừng lại!" Nhưng chẳng ai quay lại.

decisions.choice: from her days: since the city began
alternatives: Nineveh is like a pool whose waters ... (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "from the days of her", meaning that Nineveh has been like a full pool for as long as it has existed. The Greek translation reads "her waters", by a different division of the same letters: "Nineveh is like a pool of water, her waters", and some follow that reading. The sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: like a pool of water ... they flee: the city's people run out like water from a broken pool
decisions.reason: A pool full of water pictures a city full of people and wealth. Now its people pour out of it like water through a broken dam. Since water played a part in the city's fall (verse 7), the picture may be drawn from what happened.

decisions.choice: Stop! Stop!: officers calling to fleeing soldiers
decisions.reason: The shout is not assigned to a speaker; it is probably the cry of officers trying to stop the flight, which no one heeds.

decisions.choice: now its people flee (B); like water draining out (R); Someone shouts (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are. Readable makes the picture of the pool explicit (m2) and adds "Someone shouts" to introduce the cry (m3).

source.text: בֹּ֥זּוּ כֶ֖סֶף בֹּ֣זּוּ זָהָ֑ב וְאֵ֥ין קֵ֨צֶה֙ לַתְּכוּנָ֔ה כָּבֹ֕ד מִכֹּ֖ל כְּלִ֥י חֶמְדָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Plunder silver! Plunder gold! And there is no end to the supply, abundance from every article of preciousness.

en.L: Plunder silver! Plunder gold! \q And there is no end to the supply, \q wealth of every precious object.
en.B: Loot the silver! Loot the gold! \q There is no end to the treasure, \q riches of every precious kind.
en.R: Grab the silver! Grab the gold! \q There is no end to the treasure. \q The city is full of every kind of precious thing.

vi.L: Hãy cướp bạc! Hãy cướp vàng! \q Kho tàng chẳng có giới hạn, \q của cải đủ mọi vật quý giá.
vi.B: Hãy cướp lấy bạc! Hãy cướp lấy vàng! \q Kho báu nhiều vô tận, \q đủ mọi thứ của cải quý giá.
vi.R: Hãy vơ lấy bạc! Hãy vơ lấy vàng! \q Kho báu nhiều không kể xiết. \q Thành đầy dẫy đủ mọi thứ quý giá.

decisions.choice: Plunder silver! Plunder gold!: the attackers' cry
decisions.reason: The commands are the shouts of the soldiers who break in, urging one another on, or the prophet's own call to them.

decisions.choice: no end to the treasure: the wealth Assyria took from the nations
decisions.reason: Assyria grew rich on the tribute and plunder of the peoples it conquered, including Judah (2 Kings 18:14-16). Now its own treasure is plundered, as Habakkuk 2:8 says of Babylon: "Because you have plundered many nations, all the rest of the peoples will plunder you." The word translated "wealth" is the one usually rendered "glory"; here it means heaviness, abundance.

decisions.choice: Loot (B); Grab (R); riches (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the words a soldier would shout. Balanced says "riches" for the word that usually means "glory", since here it means wealth (m2).

source.text: בּוּקָ֥ה וּמְבוּקָ֖ה וּמְבֻלָּקָ֑ה וְלֵ֨ב נָמֵ֜ס וּפִ֣ק בִּרְכַּ֗יִם וְחַלְחָלָה֙ בְּכָל־מָתְנַ֔יִם וּפְנֵ֥י כֻלָּ֖ם קִבְּצ֥וּ פָארֽוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: Emptiness and emptiness and devastation! And a heart melting and tottering of knees, and anguish [is] in all loins, and the faces of all of them gather a glow.

en.L: Emptiness and desolation and devastation! \q And [the] heart melts and [the] knees knock, and anguish [is] in all loins, \q and all their faces grow pale.
en.B: Empty, emptied, stripped bare! \q Hearts melt and knees give way, every body writhes in anguish, \q and every face turns pale.
en.R: The city is empty, deserted and ruined! \q People lose their courage. Their knees shake, and their bodies are full of pain. \q Every face turns pale.

vi.L: Trống không, trống trơn và tan hoang! \q Lòng tan chảy, đầu gối run lẩy bẩy, nỗi đau quặn thắt trong mọi lưng, \q và mặt mọi người đều tái nhợt.
vi.B: Trống rỗng, trống trơn, tan hoang! \q Lòng tan chảy, gối rụng rời, thân thể ai cũng quặn đau, \q và mặt mày ai nấy đều tái xanh.
vi.R: Thành trống không, hoang vắng và đổ nát! \q Người ta mất hết can đảm. Đầu gối họ run rẩy, và thân thể họ đầy đau đớn. \q Mặt ai nấy đều tái mét.

decisions.choice: emptiness and desolation and devastation: three words that sound alike
decisions.reason: The three Hebrew words begin with the same sounds and grow longer each time, like an echo in an empty place. Isaiah 24:1-3 uses words from the same roots of the earth laid waste.

decisions.choice: heart melting, knees knocking, anguish in the loins: terror felt in the whole body
decisions.reason: A melting heart is lost courage (Joshua 2:11; Isaiah 13:7). Knees that knock and pain in the loins, the lower body, are the shaking and cramp of fear (Isaiah 21:3; Daniel 5:6).

decisions.choice: the faces of them all grow pale: the same words as Joel 2:6
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that faces "gather a glow". The phrase is used only here and in Joel 2:6. It is usually taken to mean that the color drains from them, though it could mean that they flush; either way it is the look of terror.

decisions.choice: Empty, emptied, stripped bare (B); grow pale (L), turns pale (B, R), as Joel 2:6
decisions.reason: Balanced tries to keep some of the sound play of the opening words (m1), and Readable says what they describe. The last line takes the published wording of Joel 2:6 at each level.

decisions.choice: "Trống không, trống trơn và tan hoang" (L), with alliteration for the three Hebrew words that sound alike; "mặt mọi người đều tái nhợt" (L) / "mặt mày ai nấy đều tái xanh" (B) / "Mặt ai nấy đều tái mét" (R), as the published Joel 2:6
decisions.reason: The meaning decisions: three similar-sounding words, and the same words as Joel 2:6, whose Vietnamese is reused.

source.text: אַיֵּה֙ מְע֣וֹן אֲרָי֔וֹת וּמִרְעֶ֥ה ה֖וּא לַכְּפִרִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלַךְ֩ אַרְיֵ֨ה לָבִ֥יא שָׁ֛ם גּ֥וּר אַרְיֵ֖ה וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: Where [is the] den of lions, and [the] feeding place [is] it for the young lions, where walked [the] lion, [the] lioness, there [the] cub of [the] lion, and there was no [one who] terrified [them]?

en.L: Where [is] the lions' den, \q and the pasture that [was] for the young lions, \q where the lion walked, the lioness, the lion's cub there, with no one to frighten [them]?
en.B: Where now is the lions' den, \q the place where the young lions fed, \q where the lion and lioness prowled with their cubs, and no one disturbed them?
en.R: Where is the lions' den now, \q the place where the young lions were fed? \q The lion and lioness walked there with their cubs, and nothing made them afraid.

vi.L: Hang của sư tử [ở] đâu, \q và đồng cỏ [dành] cho sư tử tơ, \q nơi sư tử đực, sư tử cái, sư tử con dạo bước, chẳng ai làm [chúng] sợ hãi?
vi.B: Bây giờ hang sư tử ở đâu, \q nơi sư tử tơ được nuôi ăn, \q nơi sư tử đực và sư tử cái đi lại với đàn con, chẳng ai quấy rầy?
vi.R: Bây giờ hang sư tử ở đâu, \q nơi sư tử tơ được nuôi ăn? \q Sư tử đực và sư tử cái đã từng đi lại ở đó với đàn con, và chẳng có gì làm chúng sợ.

decisions.choice: where is the lions' den?: Nineveh, home of the lion that preyed on the nations
decisions.reason: The question is a taunt: the den is gone. The lion stands for the kings of Assyria and the city is their den. Assyrian kings showed themselves as lion hunters and compared themselves to lions, and Nineveh's palaces were decorated with lions. The picture runs to verse 14.

decisions.choice: the lion, the lioness, the young lions and the cub
decisions.reason: Hebrew has several words for lions, by age and sex. The second word may be "lioness" or another word for a lion; the poem uses them all to picture the whole royal family of beasts living without fear.

decisions.choice: the question placed first; nothing made them afraid
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the question at the start and then says what the den was like in a separate sentence.

source.text: אַרְיֵ֤ה טֹרֵף֙ בְּדֵ֣י גֹֽרוֹתָ֔יו וּמְחַנֵּ֖ק לְלִבְאֹתָ֑יו וַיְמַלֵּא־טֶ֣רֶף חֹרָ֔יו וּמְעֹֽנֹתָ֖יו טְרֵפָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] lion was tearing for [the] sufficiency of his cubs, and was strangling for his lionesses; and he filled with prey his holes, and his dens [with] torn flesh.

en.L: The lion tore enough for his cubs, \q and strangled [prey] for his lionesses, \q and he filled his holes with prey, \q and his dens with torn flesh.
en.B: The lion killed enough for his cubs \q and strangled prey for his mates; \q he filled his caves with prey \q and his dens with what he had torn.
en.R: The lion killed enough food for his cubs. \q He strangled animals for his mates. \q He filled his caves with what he had killed, \q and his dens with torn-up meat.

vi.L: Sư tử xé mồi đủ cho đàn con nó, \q và bóp cổ [mồi] cho các sư tử cái nó, \q và nó chất đầy hang nó với mồi, \q và ổ nó với thịt xé.
vi.B: Sư tử giết đủ mồi cho đàn con \q và bóp cổ con mồi cho các sư tử cái; \q nó chất đầy hang mình bằng mồi \q và ổ mình bằng thịt xé.
vi.R: Sư tử giết đủ thức ăn cho đàn con. \q Nó bóp cổ thú vật cho các sư tử cái. \q Nó chất đầy hang bằng những con mồi đã giết, \q và chất đầy ổ bằng thịt bị xé nát.

decisions.choice: the lion's prey: what Assyria took from the nations
decisions.reason: The lion brings home prey for his family; Assyria brought the plunder of conquered peoples home to Nineveh. "Torn prey" returns in 3:1, where the city is "never without prey".

decisions.choice: strangled [prey] (L); strangled prey (B); strangled animals (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves the object of "strangled" unstated; Literal brackets it. The two words for torn prey are rendered "prey" and "torn flesh" or "what he had torn".

source.text: הִנְנִ֣י אֵלַ֗יִךְ נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְהִבְעַרְתִּ֤י בֶֽעָשָׁן֙ רִכְבָּ֔הּ וּכְפִירַ֖יִךְ תֹּ֣אכַל חָ֑רֶב וְהִכְרַתִּ֤י מֵאֶ֨רֶץ֙ טַרְפֵּ֔ךְ וְלֹֽא־יִשָּׁמַ֥ע ע֖וֹד ק֥וֹל מַלְאָכֵֽכֵה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Here I [am] against you, declaration of Yahweh of hosts, and I will burn in smoke her chariots, and your young lions will devour [the] sword; and I will cut off from [the] earth your prey, and not will be heard again [the] voice of your messengers.

en.L: Look, I [am] against you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q and I will burn her chariots in smoke, \q and [the] sword will eat up your young lions; \q and I will cut your prey off from the land, \q and the voice of your messengers will not be heard again.
en.B: I am against you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q I will burn up your chariots in a cloud of smoke, \q and the sword will feed on your young lions. \q I will leave you no prey on the earth, \q and your messengers' voices will be heard no more.
en.R: I am against you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q I will burn up your chariots, and they will go up in smoke. \q Your young soldiers will be killed in battle. \q You will hunt no more prey on the earth. \q No one will ever again hear the voices of your messengers.

vi.L: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chống lại ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán vậy, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đốt xe chiến mã của nó trong khói, \q gươm sẽ ăn nuốt các sư tử tơ của ngươi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cất mồi của ngươi khỏi đất, \q và tiếng của các sứ giả ngươi sẽ không còn được nghe nữa.
vi.B: Ta chống lại ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán vậy. \q Ta sẽ thiêu rụi xe chiến mã của ngươi trong đám khói, \q và gươm sẽ ăn nuốt các sư tử tơ của ngươi. \q Ta sẽ không để cho ngươi còn mồi trên đất, \q và tiếng của các sứ giả ngươi sẽ không còn nghe thấy nữa.
vi.R: Ta chống lại ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. \q Ta sẽ thiêu rụi xe chiến mã của ngươi, và chúng sẽ bốc thành khói. \q Các chiến binh trẻ của ngươi sẽ chết trận. \q Ngươi sẽ không còn săn mồi trên đất nữa. \q Sẽ không ai còn nghe tiếng các sứ giả của ngươi nữa.

decisions.choice: I am against you, declares the LORD of hosts: the LORD declares himself Nineveh's enemy
decisions.reason: The formula announces that the LORD is coming against someone as an enemy (Jeremiah 21:13; 50:31; Ezekiel 5:8). Nahum uses it here and again in 3:5. The LORD of hosts is the LORD who commands the armies of heaven and earth.

decisions.choice: her chariots: the switch from "you" to "her"
decisions.reason: The verse speaks to Nineveh as "you" but says "her chariots". Such shifts between speaking to and about someone are common in Hebrew poetry (Isaiah 5:8). Some read "your chariots" with a small change. The chariots are Nineveh's either way.

decisions.choice: the voice of your messengers: Assyria's envoys
decisions.reason: Assyrian kings sent envoys to demand surrender and tribute, as Sennacherib's officials did at the walls of Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17-35; 19:9-13). That voice will be silent.

decisions.choice: Look, I [am] against you, declares the LORD of hosts (L); I am against you, declares the LORD of Armies (B); says the LORD of Armies (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the formula, as in Jeremiah 50:31. Balanced and Readable leave out "Look".

decisions.choice: your chariots (B, R); Your young soldiers (R); hunt no more prey (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "your chariots" so that the verse speaks to Nineveh throughout; the Hebrew has "her" (m2). Readable says what the young lions stand for, the city's young fighting men, and keeps the picture of the hunt.

decisions.choice: "Ta chống lại ngươi, CHÚA Vạn Quân phán vậy" (L, B); "... CHÚA Vạn Quân phán" (R)
decisions.reason: The Isaiah note's "phán vậy" (L, B) / "phán" (R) for "ne'um", with "CHÚA Vạn Quân" spanned on CHÚA only. Literal keeps the Hebrew's switch to "her chariots" ("của nó"), as the meaning decision notes.
